NOUGHTS AND CROSSES — KEYS AND TIMING

We read the original BASIC lines 6000–6080 and played two turns in Fuse 1.6.0 on the 48K machine.

At the prompt, enter two digits without a space: row, then column. Both digits must be 1, 2, or 3. Press Enter to submit. The human marks X; the computer marks O. We entered 11, then 22, and saw different board positions after both accepted moves.

Run from the repository root:
  sh src/assets/basic-src/original-sinclair-basic-collections/Granada-Publishing/09-noughts-and-crosses/BASIC/REPLAY.sh

Fuse runs at 100% speed. Waits below use wall-clock seconds.

  1. Open the original TAP with the 48K ROM and automatic tape loading.
  2. Wait 3 seconds; type 1, 1, Enter, holding each key for 0.2 seconds.
  3. Wait 15 seconds for the computer's reply; save 01-AFTER-11.png.
  4. Type 2, 2, Enter with the same holds.
  5. Wait 15 seconds for the reply; save 02-AFTER-22.png.

The run checks changed pixels inside the board. It shows two human turns and the replies, not a full match. The computer takes its time; the tape supplies no fast-forward button.
